intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that spondylometaphyseal dysplasia of the Sedaghatian type (SMDS) is caused by compound heterozygous mutation in the GPX4 gene. In a second family, both unaffected parents of an affected child carried the same heterozygous truncating GPX4 mutation, but DNA from the child was not available.

checks.claim: Spondylometaphyseal dysplasia of the Sedaghatian type (SMDS) is caused by compound heterozygous mutation in the GPX4 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Whole exome sequencing of a child affected with SSMD and her unaffected parents identified two rare variants in GPX4. The first (c.587+5G>A) was inherited from the mother, and the second (c.588-8_588-4del) was de novo
checks.explanation: The abstract reports two GPX4 variants in one child, one maternal and one de novo, but it never says 'compound heterozygous' or confirms the phase. In the second family the child would be expected to be homozygous, not compound heterozygous.

checks.claim: In a second SMDS family, both unaffected parents of an affected child carried the same heterozygous truncating GPX4 mutation.
checks.evidence_quote: the two unaffected parents were found by Sanger sequencing to each carry the same heterozygous stop mutation in exon 3 of GPX4, c.381C>A, p.Tyr127*
checks.explanation: A stop mutation is a truncating mutation.

checks.claim: In the second SMDS family, DNA from the affected child was not available.
checks.evidence_quote: although DNA from the child was not available

paragraphs.text: Sedaghatian (1980) reported 2 brothers, born within a year of each other, with a skeletal disorder of severe congenital metaphyseal involvement, mild rhizomelic shortness of the upper limbs, and mild platyspondyly. Both died at 3 days of cardiorespiratory insufficiency. Only 1 had antemortem laboratory tests, which showed low calcium, high phosphorus, and high alkaline phosphatase levels, attributed to a renal defect. At autopsy, this infant had pulmonary, renal, and adrenal hemorrhage, as well as subendocardial myocarditis and myocardial necrosis. The parents were normal and had recently had an affected baby girl.

paragraphs.text: Koutouby et al. (2000) reported an infant born to nonconsanguineous Yemeni parents with radiologic findings consistent with the Sedaghatian type of lethal metaphyseal chondrodysplasia. Whereas all previously reported cases had died within 4 days of life, this patient survived 161 days. Investigations included serum calcium, magnesium, zinc, ammonia, phosphate, alkaline phosphatase, and parathormone levels, liver and renal function tests, TORCH, metabolic screening, chromosome studies, muscle enzymes, EEG, and CT and MRI of the brain. Genomic DNA analysis of the patient and parents did not detect an abnormal gene.

(2006) reported a female infant, born to nonconsanguineous Caucasian parents, with metaphyseal dysplasia and a neuronal migration abnormality consistent with Sedaghatian spondylometaphyseal dysplasia. She developed seizures on day 14 and died at 17 days of age.

paragraphs.text: As part of the FORGE Canada Consortium, Smith et al. (2014) studied 2 unrelated families with Sedaghatian-type spondylometaphyseal dysplasia. Whole-exome sequencing of an affected girl and her unaffected parents identified compound heterozygous variants in the GPX4 gene: c.587+5G-A, inherited from the mother, and c.588-8_588-4del, which arose de novo. Both were predicted to affect splicing; in vitro studies confirmed that the first mutation spliced out part of exon 4 and the second caused skipping of exon 5, each resulting in a frameshift and premature truncation of GPX4. In a second family, DNA from the affected child was not available, but Sanger sequencing showed that both unaffected parents carried the same heterozygous nonsense mutation in exon 3 of GPX4, c.381C-A, resulting in a tyr127-to-ter (Y127X) substitution.

paragraphs.text: In a girl with Sedaghatian-type spondylometaphyseal dysplasia, Smith et al. (2014) identified a de novo 5-bp deletion (c.588-8_588-4del) in the GPX4 gene, in compound heterozygosity with a maternally inherited c.587+5G-A mutation. In vitro studies showed that the deletion caused skipping of exon 5, resulting in a frameshift and premature truncation of GPX4.

checks.claim: Smith et al. (2014) identified a de novo 5-bp deletion in GPX4, c.588-8_588-4del, in a girl with Sedaghatian-type spondylometaphyseal dysplasia.
checks.evidence_quote: the second (c.588-8_588-4del) was de novo
checks.explanation: The deletion spans 5 bp; the child is female ('her').

checks.claim: The GPX4 c.588-8_588-4del deletion was in compound heterozygosity with a maternally inherited c.587+5G-A mutation in the girl reported by Smith et al. (2014).
checks.evidence_quote: The first (c.587+5G>A) was inherited from the mother, and the second (c.588-8_588-4del) was de novo
checks.explanation: Both variants and their origins are stated, but the abstract does not explicitly confirm compound heterozygosity (phase).

checks.claim: In vitro studies showed that the GPX4 c.588-8_588-4del deletion caused skipping of exon 5, resulting in a frameshift and premature truncation of GPX4.
checks.evidence_quote: In vitro studies confirmed the mutations spliced out part of exon 4 and skipped exon 5, respectively, with both resulting in a frameshift and premature truncation of GPX4.
checks.explanation: Exon 5 skipping is assigned to the second variant, the deletion.

paragraphs.text: In a family with a child with Sedaghatian-type spondylometaphyseal dysplasia whose DNA was not available, Smith et al. (2014) found by Sanger sequencing that both unaffected parents carried the same heterozygous c.381C-A transversion in exon 3 of the GPX4 gene, resulting in a tyr127-to-ter (Y127X) substitution.

checks.claim: In a family with a child with Sedaghatian-type spondylometaphyseal dysplasia studied by Smith et al. (2014), the child's DNA was not available.
checks.evidence_quote: although DNA from the child was not available

checks.claim: Smith et al. (2014) found by Sanger sequencing that both unaffected parents of a child with Sedaghatian-type spondylometaphyseal dysplasia carried the same heterozygous GPX4 c.381C-A transversion.
checks.evidence_quote: the two unaffected parents were found by Sanger sequencing to each carry the same heterozygous stop mutation in exon 3 of GPX4, c.381C>A

checks.claim: The GPX4 c.381C-A transversion is in exon 3 and results in a tyr127-to-ter (Y127X) substitution.
checks.evidence_quote: heterozygous stop mutation in exon 3 of GPX4, c.381C>A, p.Tyr127*
checks.explanation: p.Tyr127* is the same as Y127X.

agent.process_note: I read all 8 papers listed in the index. Every one is available only as an abstract. GPX4 is identified as the causal gene by Smith et al. (2014) alone. Its MIM number and chromosomal location were not in the reference data (none was supplied), so I left them out of the intro. Homozygosity was not shown directly in any patient: in the second family of Smith et al. (2014) only the parents were tested, so the intro gives compound heterozygosity and the text describes the second family as it was reported. Patient-level details that would be in the full texts, such as Peeden et al.'s patient, the 2 cases of Elcioglu and Hall, and further clinical information from Smith et al., were not available.
